about.title: Clearlake Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Clearlake's economy runs on a mix of small businesses, agriculture, service work, and roadside operations along corridors like Lakeshore Drive and Rt 53, and workplace injuries here can happen anywhere from a job site to a delivery route. Most people assume workers' compensation is their only option after getting hurt on the job, and in many cases it is the exclusive remedy against an employer. But if a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside comp benefits. Reporting an injury to your employer within 30 days is required to protect your workers' comp rights, and California law prohibits retaliation for doing so. LawProactive connects injured workers in Clearlake with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at the full picture, including whether a third party bears responsibility, and explain the options available under a contingency arrangement.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be pursued separately for additional recovery.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries its own 2-year statute of limitations, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Exists
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim, and an attorney can help you understand what that protection covers.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Old Highway 53 by a contractor's equipment — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: You may be able to do both. Workers' comp typically covers your medical care and lost wages regardless of fault, while a separate claim against the equipment owner or subcontractor, if they were negligent, could address damages comp doesn't cover. An independent attorney can review the details and explain how the two claims might work together.

items.question: What if my employer in Clearlake tells me not to report my injury?
items.answer: That's not something an employer can legally require. California law gives you a window, generally 30 days, to report a workplace injury, and retaliating against you for doing so is illegal. An attorney can advise you on documenting the injury properly even if your employer discourages it.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service is completely free. Attorneys in the network generally work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You're never obligated to hire anyone you're connected with.
